newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWIMMING-FROLANDER WINS 100 METRES BUTTERFLY WORLD TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-FROLANDER WINS 100 METRES BUTTERFLY WORLD TITLE.

text.p: Lars Frolander claimed the first title of the world short-course swimming championships for hosts Sweden when he won the men's 100 metres butterfly on Thursday.
Frolander was awarded victory after a mix-up on the electronic scoreboard had originally made him second behind Australia's Michael Klim.
Klim was initially credited with a time of 50.13 seconds, which would have been nearly two seconds inside the world record.
But after a few minutes the times were rejigged and home Swedish fans roared their approval when Frolander was revealed as the winner in 51.95 seconds.
Australian Geoff Huegill took the silver in 51.99 and Klim, who had set the pace over the first 50 metres, had to settle for the bronze in a revised 52.02 ahead of Britain's James Hickman ( 52.22).
Frolander, the fastest qualifier, trailed sixth of the eight finalists at the halfway point of the race in a specially built 25-metre pool in the Scandinavium indoor arena.
Olympic champion Denis Pankratov of Russia failed to qualify for the final, having finished a well-beaten fifth in his morning heat and 11th overall.
Pankratov's heat time of 53.48 seconds was way outside his 51.78 world short-course record set in Paris at a World Cup meet in February.
He won the consolation "B" final in 52.48, which would have left him fifth in the main final.
